title: Third Largest Distinct Value
statement:
You get an integer array nums. Return the third largest distinct value in it: repeated values count once.

If there are fewer than three distinct values, return the largest value instead. Aim for a single pass with O(1) extra memory.

examples.why: Duplicates count once: 8, 6, 2. Sorting and taking the third item from the end would give 6.
Only two distinct values, so the answer falls back to the largest.

hints: Sorting works but is O(n log n). Can you keep just the top three while scanning?
Keep first, second and third as the three largest distinct values seen so far, using a null-like marker for empty slots.
Skip any value equal to one already kept. Otherwise shift it into the right slot. Watch out: the smallest possible int is a legal value, so it cannot be the empty marker.

explain.intuition:
You only ever need the three biggest distinct values, so keep three slots and update them as you scan, like keeping a podium of the top three scores. A new value that ties a podium value changes nothing. A new value bigger than the first place pushes everyone down one step, and so on.

The subtle part is the empty slot. The input can contain the smallest 32-bit integer, so using it as "nothing here yet" would confuse a real value with an empty slot. Use null in JavaScript and None in Python, or -Infinity, which no integer can equal.
steps: For each x: if it equals a, b or c, skip it.
If x > a: shift to c = b, b = a, a = x. Else if x > b: c = b, b = x. Else if x > c: c = x.
Return c if it was filled, otherwise a.
pitfalls: Counting duplicates: in [8, 8, 6] the third largest distinct value does not exist, so the answer is 8, not 6.
Using -2147483648 as the empty marker. Then [1, 2, -2147483648] looks like it has only two values.
Forgetting the fallback: with fewer than three distinct values, return the maximum, not the second largest.

solutions.title: Sort the distinct values
solutions.idea: Put the values in a set, sort them in descending order, and pick the third one or the first.

solutions.title: Three slots in one pass
solutions.idea: Keep the top three distinct values seen so far, with -Infinity as the empty marker, and shift them down when a bigger value arrives.

followups: Generalise to the k-th largest distinct value. What structure replaces the three slots?
Would a heap of size 3 work here? How do you keep duplicates out of it?
